chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Malik ibn Atiyya, from Yunus ibn 'Ammar, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'May I be sacrificed for you! This, which has appeared on my face, the people allege that Allah has not afflicted a servant with it in whom He has a need.'
He (peace be upon him) said: 'No. The Believer of the Pharaoh's household was of crippled fingers, so he would say like this,' and he extended his hand and said: 'O people! Follow the Messengers.'

He said: 'Then he said to me: When it is the last third of the night during its beginning, perform ablution, then stand for your prayer which you tend to pray. So when you are in the last prostration from the first two rak'at, say while you are prostrating:'
'O Ali, O Magnificent, O Beneficent, O Merciful, O Hearer of the supplications, O Giver of goodness! Send blessings upon Muhammad and the People of the Household of Muhammad.'
And give me from the goodness of the world and the Hereafter whatever You deem to be rightful, and turn away from me from the evil of the world and the Hereafter what I am deserving of.
And remove from me this pain' – and you specify it – 'for it has anguished me and grieved me' – and insist in the supplication.'
He said: 'So I did it, and I had not even arrived in Kufa until Allah had removed all of it from me.'

key_terms.الثُّلُثُ الْأَخِيرُ مِنَ اللَّيْلِ: The last third of the night

ai.seo_question: What is the specific supplication and prayer method for healing a physical ailment according to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates the concept of divine testing through physical affliction by citing the 'Believer of Pharaoh's Family' (Surah Ghafir), whose fingers were cut off yet he remained steadfast, thereby encouraging patience during illness. The prescribed ritual emphasizes the spiritual potency of the last third of the night (Qada' al-Hajah) and the specific efficacy of supplication during the final prostration (Sajdah) of the Fajr prayer, linking physical healing to spiritual devotion and the intercession of the Ahl al-Bayt.
